stem.en:
Kamola's little brother usually talks from morning till night, asking question after question. On his first day at his new school, however, he sat in a corner of the classroom and said almost nothing. His parents were surprised to see him so ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: quiet
cheerful
curious
talkative

why.en: The clue is 'however' and 'said almost nothing': that day he was quiet. 'Talkative' is how he usually is, the opposite of the clue.
why.uz: Ishora — «however» va «said almost nothing»: oʻsha kuni u jim boʻlgan. «Talkative» — uning odatdagi holati, ishoraga zid.
why.ru: Подсказка — «however» и «said almost nothing»: в тот день он молчал. «Talkative» — его обычное состояние, это против подсказки.

stem.en:
The museum's new map quickly became popular with visitors. Before, people often got lost in the long halls; the new map shows each floor in a different color and marks every exit clearly. Most visitors now describe it as ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: easy to use
hard to read
too small
out of date

why.en: A color for each floor and clearly marked exits make the map easy to use. 'Hard to read' goes against the clue, and the map is new, not out of date.
why.uz: Har bir qavat uchun rang va aniq chiqish joylari xaritani «easy to use» qiladi. «Hard to read» ishoraga zid, xarita esa yangi, eskirgan emas.
why.ru: Цвет для каждого этажа и ясно отмеченные выходы делают карту «easy to use». «Hard to read» против подсказки, а карта новая, не устаревшая.

stem.en:
Many readers expected the second book in the series to repeat the first: another quiet story set in the same small village. Instead, the author moved her characters to a busy port city and filled the plot with storms, chases and surprises. Reviewers called the change ______.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: daring
predictable
minor
unnoticed

why.en: 'Instead' shows that the author did the opposite of what readers expected, a big risk: 'daring'. 'Predictable' and 'minor' go against that.
why.uz: «Instead» muallif kutilganning aksini qilganini koʻrsatadi — bu katta tavakkal: «daring». «Predictable» va «minor» bunga zid.
why.ru: «Instead» показывает, что автор сделала обратное ожидаемому, — это большой риск: «daring». «Predictable» и «minor» этому противоречат.

stem.en:
The following text is from a short story.

When the power went out, the whole building fell silent. Aziz lit a candle and set it on the table, and its small flame drew his younger sisters out of the dark corners of the room until all three of them sat close together, watching it.

As used in the text, what does the word "drew" most nearly mean?

options.en: attracted
sketched
inhaled
chose at random

why.en: The flame made the girls come out of the corners and sit near it, so 'drew' means 'attracted'. Sketching and breathing do not fit.
why.uz: Olov qizlarni burchaklardan chiqarib, yoniga oʻtqazdi, demak, «drew» — «attracted» (oʻziga tortdi). Chizish yoki nafas olish mos emas.
why.ru: Пламя заставило девочек выйти из углов и сесть рядом, значит, «drew» — «attracted» (привлекло). «Рисовать» и «вдыхать» не подходят.

stem.en:
Critics of the city's new library had predicted that its glass walls would make the reading rooms too bright and too hot. A year after the opening, however, their worries seem ______: thanks to blinds that lower themselves in strong sunlight, the rooms have stayed cool and comfortable even in July.

Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

options.en: unfounded
justified
understated
urgent

why.en: The rooms stayed cool, so what happened did not support the worries: 'unfounded'. 'Justified' is the opposite; 'understated' would mean things were worse.
why.uz: Xonalar salqin qoldi, demak, tanqidchilarning xavotiri asossiz chiqdi: «unfounded». «Justified» — aksi; «understated» esa vaziyat yomonroq degani boʻlardi.
why.ru: В залах прохладно, значит, опасения не подтвердились: «unfounded». «Justified» — наоборот, а «understated» значило бы, что всё ещё хуже.

stem.en:
Every Friday after school, Mr. Yusupov keeps his science classroom open for an extra hour. Students can come to finish experiments, ask questions about homework or simply look through the microscopes. Last month so many students came that he had to bring in extra chairs from the hall.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To describe a popular after-school hour in a classroom
To explain how microscopes help students see small objects
To complain that the school does not have enough chairs
To argue that homework should be done only at school

why.en: The text describes the open hour and ends with how many students come. Chairs and microscopes are details; nothing argues or complains.
why.uz: Matn ochiq soatni tasvirlaydi va qancha oʻquvchi kelishi bilan tugaydi. Stullar va mikroskoplar — tafsilot; hech kim bahslashmaydi yoki shikoyat qilmaydi.
why.ru: Текст описывает свободный час и кончается тем, сколько учеников приходит. Стулья и микроскопы — детали; никто не спорит и не жалуется.

stem.en:
Dilshod was sure that his old bicycle was too slow for the long ride to his uncle's village. Then a neighbor showed him how to pump up the tires and oil the chain. The next weekend, Dilshod made the trip in half the time he had expected.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It presents a worry, describes a simple fix and then shows its result.
It describes a village and then explains why people move away from it.
It compares two bicycles and then recommends the faster one.
It lists the steps for building a bicycle from separate parts.

why.en: Sentence 1 is the worry (too slow), sentence 2 is the fix (tires and chain), and sentence 3 is the result (half the time).
why.uz: 1-gap — xavotir (juda sekin), 2-gap — yechim (shinalar va zanjir), 3-gap — natija (yarim vaqtda).
why.ru: Предложение 1 — тревога (слишком медленный), 2 — решение (шины и цепь), 3 — результат (вдвое быстрее).

stem.en:
Some games can teach useful skills. In one board game that Nodira plays with her cousins, players buy and sell goods and must keep track of their money at every turn. After a few months of playing, Nodira found that she could add up prices in her head much faster than before.

Which choice best describes the function of the second sentence in the text as a whole?

options.en: It gives a specific example of the claim made in the first sentence.
It argues that board games are better than video games.
It explains why Nodira's cousins do not enjoy playing the game with her.
It describes a problem that the last sentence then solves.

why.en: Sentence 1 makes a general claim (games teach skills); sentence 2 names one game where players handle money, an example of that claim.
why.uz: 1-gap umumiy daʼvo (oʻyinlar koʻnikma beradi); 2-gap oʻyinchilar pul bilan ishlaydigan bitta oʻyinni aytadi — bu daʼvoga misol.
why.ru: Предложение 1 — общее утверждение (игры учат навыкам); 2 называет игру, где игроки считают деньги, — пример этого утверждения.

The city's bus company has added something new to its stops. A small screen at each stop now shows how many minutes are left until the next bus arrives. Riders no longer have to guess whether they have time to buy a snack or should stay and wait.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To describe a new feature at bus stops and how it helps riders
To explain why the city's buses are often late
To compare the city's buses with other kinds of transport, such as trains and taxis
To encourage riders to buy snacks while they wait for buses

stem.en:
For many years, the people of a small mountain town believed that the old stone wall above their houses had been built to keep out wolves. When a local teacher studied the town's old records, however, she found letters that described the wall's real purpose: it had been built to stop snow from sliding down onto the houses in winter.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It describes a common belief and then presents evidence that corrects it.
It describes a problem in the town and then explains why no one has ever been able to solve it.
It compares two walls and then explains which one was built first.
It tells how a teacher became famous for her discovery.

why.en: First comes what people believed (the wall kept out wolves), then the letters that show its real purpose (stopping snow). The belief is corrected.
why.uz: Avval odamlar nimaga ishongani (devor boʻrilardan himoya qilgan), keyin asl maqsadni koʻrsatgan maktublar (qorni toʻxtatish). Ishonch tuzatiladi.
why.ru: Сначала то, во что верили люди (стена от волков), затем письма о настоящей цели (удерживать снег). Прежнее мнение исправлено.

stem.en:
Many people assume that a silent library is the best place to study. For some students, though, complete silence makes every small sound, such as a cough or a turning page, more distracting. These students often focus better with gentle background noise, like the low hum of a busy café.

Which choice best describes the function of the second sentence in the text as a whole?

options.en: It challenges the assumption described in the first sentence.
It gives an example that supports the first sentence.
It describes the rules that libraries set for their visitors.
It explains why cafés are louder than libraries.

why.en: Sentence 1 states a common belief; 'though' in sentence 2 signals a challenge: for some students, silence makes small sounds more distracting.
why.uz: 1-gap keng tarqalgan fikrni aytadi; 2-gapdagi «though» eʼtirozni bildiradi: baʼzi oʻquvchilarga sukunatda kichik tovushlar koʻproq xalaqit beradi.
why.ru: Предложение 1 — распространённое мнение; «though» во 2-м сигналит возражение: некоторым ученикам в тишине мелкие звуки мешают сильнее.

stem.en:
When Rustam's family moved into their new apartment, the only furniture in the living room was a heavy wooden table left by the previous owners. His mother wanted to sell it, but his father insisted on keeping it. Over the years, that table held birthday cakes, school projects and late-night card games, and no one ever mentioned selling it again.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To show how an object that was almost sold became part of family life
To explain how to choose furniture for a new apartment
To describe an argument that divided a family for many years
To criticize the previous owners for leaving their old furniture behind in the apartment

why.en: The text follows the table from 'almost sold' to the center of family events. The disagreement is short, and no one is criticized.
why.uz: Matn stolning «sotilay degan» holatdan oilaviy voqealar markaziga aylanishini kuzatadi. Bahs qisqa, hech kim tanqid qilinmaydi.
why.ru: Текст ведёт стол от «чуть не продали» до центра семейных событий. Спор короткий, и никого не критикуют.

stem.en:
Oybek, the class leader, had planned the class trip for weeks: the bus was booked, the tickets were printed, and every student had a seat. On the morning of the trip, the bus driver called to say that the bus would not start. Oybek looked at the thirty students waiting at the school gate and picked up his phone again.

Which choice best describes the function of the second sentence in the text as a whole?

options.en: It brings in a problem that threatens the careful plans.
It explains why Oybek spent weeks planning the trip.
It describes how the students finally reached the trip's destination.
It shows that Oybek had forgotten to book a bus for the trip.

why.en: Sentence 1 shows careful plans; sentence 2 brings a problem (the bus will not start). The bus was booked, so he did not forget it.
why.uz: 1-gap puxta rejalarni koʻrsatadi; 2-gap muammo olib keladi (avtobus yurmaydi). Avtobus band qilingan edi, demak, u unutmagan.
why.ru: Предложение 1 показывает тщательные планы; 2 приносит проблему (автобус не заводится). Автобус был заказан, так что он не забыл.

stem.en:
Critics of homework often argue that it simply takes time away from rest and play. That argument has some force when homework is long and repetitive. Yet a short task that asks students to explain one idea in their own words can show a teacher exactly where a lesson went wrong, information that a quiet classroom rarely reveals.

Which choice best describes the overall structure of the text?

options.en: It grants part of a criticism, then points to a kind of homework that is useful.
It states a criticism of homework and then argues that all homework should be abolished at once.
It describes a teacher's method and then explains why the method failed.
It compares two classrooms and then recommends giving longer homework.

why.en: Sentence 1 gives the critics' view, sentence 2 accepts it for long tasks ('some force'), and 'Yet' brings in short tasks that help teachers.
why.uz: 1-gap tanqidchilar fikri, 2-gap uni uzun vazifalar uchun qabul qiladi («some force»), «Yet» esa oʻqituvchiga yordam beradigan qisqa vazifani kiritadi.
why.ru: Предложение 1 — мнение критиков, 2 принимает его для длинных заданий («some force»), а «Yet» вводит короткие задания, полезные учителю.

stem.en:
Old maps of the region show a lake where today there is only dry, cracked ground. Farmers who were children when the water was still there describe fishing boats and summer swimming. Their memories matter: without them, a young visitor walking across the dry plain might never guess that a lake had ever been there.

Which choice best describes the function of the last sentence in the text as a whole?

options.en: It explains why the farmers' memories of the lake are valuable.
It argues that the lake will return if farmers use less water.
It describes what visitors usually do when they cross the plain.
It questions whether the old maps of the region are accurate.

why.en: 'Their memories matter', and the rest of the sentence gives the reason: without them, no one would guess that a lake was there.
why.uz: «Their memories matter» deyiladi, gapning qolgan qismi sababini beradi: ularsiz bu yerda koʻl boʻlganini hech kim taxmin qilmasdi.
why.ru: Сказано «Their memories matter», а остаток фразы даёт причину: без них никто бы не догадался, что здесь было озеро.

stem.en:
The following text is from a poem.

My father's watch no longer keeps the hour;
its hands have rested at ten past two for years.
Still, every morning, he winds it once,
holds it to his ear, and smiles
as if the silence told him something true.

Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

options.en: To show that a broken object still holds meaning for the person who keeps it
To explain how to repair an old watch that has stopped working
To express the speaker's frustration with a father who is always late for every family event
To argue that old objects should be replaced once they stop working

why.en: The watch has stopped, yet ('Still') the father winds it and smiles: the poem shows the broken watch matters to him. Nothing is repaired or argued.
why.uz: Soat toʻxtagan, lekin («Still») ota uni buraydi va jilmayadi: sheʼr singan soat unga qadrli ekanini koʻrsatadi. Hech narsa taʼmirlanmaydi.
why.ru: Часы стоят, но («Still») отец заводит их и улыбается: стихотворение показывает, что сломанные часы ему дороги. Их не чинят.

stem.en:
Text 1
Several parents in our district want the school day to begin an hour later. Teenagers, they point out, tend to fall asleep late, so an eight o'clock start leaves many of them tired in their first lessons.

Text 2
A later start sounds kind, but the school day would then end later too. Students who work, look after younger brothers and sisters, or travel to sports training in the afternoon would lose time that they cannot easily get back.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the parents' proposal in Text 1?

options.en: By warning that a later start would create new problems in the afternoon
By agreeing that the school day should begin an hour later
By arguing that teenagers need less sleep than parents think
By suggesting that sports training should take place before school instead

why.en: Text 2 says a later start 'sounds kind, but' the day would end later, costing students afternoon time for work, family and sport.
why.uz: Text 2 kechroq boshlash «sounds kind, but» kun ham kechroq tugaydi deydi: oʻquvchilar ish, oila va sport uchun tushdan keyingi vaqtni yoʻqotadi.
why.ru: Text 2: поздний старт «sounds kind, but» день кончится позже, и ученики потеряют время после обеда на работу, семью и спорт.

stem.en:
Text 1
The town museum now lets visitors handle copies of old objects: a wooden plow, a clay lamp, a spinning wheel. Holding an object, the curator says, teaches more than any label behind glass.

Text 2
The museum's new hands-on room is popular, but some visitors complain that it is noisy and crowded and that they cannot read the labels in peace. They would like quiet hours when the room is closed to school groups.

Which choice best describes how Text 1 and Text 2 differ?

options.en: Text 1 praises handling objects; Text 2 reports problems in the room.
Text 1 opposes the hands-on room, while Text 2 supports it.
Text 1 describes the museum's past, while Text 2 describes its future plans.
Text 1 and Text 2 both argue that the room should be closed to all visitors.

why.en: Text 1 gives the curator's reason for handling objects (it teaches more); Text 2 reports visitors' complaints about noise and crowds.
why.uz: Text 1 buyumlarni ushlab koʻrish foydasini aytadi (koʻproq oʻrgatadi); Text 2 shovqin va tiqilinch haqidagi shikoyatlarni keltiradi.
why.ru: Text 1 называет пользу того, чтобы держать предметы в руках (это учит больше); Text 2 передаёт жалобы на шум и толпу.

stem.en:
Text 1
Mr. Rahimov asks his students to take notes by hand. Writing is slower than typing, he admits, but that is exactly the point: because students cannot copy down every word, they must decide what matters and put it in their own words.

Text 2
For students who write slowly or whose handwriting is hard to read, notes taken by hand can be a burden. Typing lets them keep up with the lesson and read their notes later. A teacher who insists on handwriting may help some students while leaving others behind.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Mr. Rahimov's rule in Text 1?

options.en: By pointing out that the rule may not suit every student, even if it helps some
By agreeing that every student should take notes only by hand
By arguing that typing helps students decide what matters most
By claiming that most students never read any of their notes again after a lesson has ended

why.en: Text 2 ends: handwriting 'may help some students while leaving others behind'. It does not reject the rule for all; it says it does not suit everyone.
why.uz: Text 2 oxirida qoʻlda yozish «may help some students while leaving others behind» deydi: qoida hammaga ham mos emas.
why.ru: Text 2 заканчивается так: письмо от руки «may help some students while leaving others behind», то есть правило подходит не всем.

stem.en:
Text 1
The old cinema on Bahor Street has stood empty for ten years. The council now wants to pull it down and build a sports hall, which the neighborhood badly needs.

Text 2
The cinema's carved front and high ceiling could never be built again. Instead of pulling it down, the council could turn the inside into a sports hall and keep the old walls. The neighborhood does need a place for sport, but not at the cost of its oldest building.

Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

options.en: The neighborhood needs a place for sport.
The old cinema should be pulled down.
The cinema should start showing films again.
The council has no plans for the building.

why.en: Text 1 says the area 'badly needs' a sports hall; Text 2 says it 'does need a place for sport'. They disagree only about pulling the cinema down.
why.uz: Text 1 hududga sport zali «badly needs» deydi; Text 2 ham «does need a place for sport» deydi. Ular faqat kinoteatrni buzishda kelishmaydi.
why.ru: Text 1: району «badly needs» спортзал; Text 2: «does need a place for sport». Они расходятся только в том, сносить ли кинотеатр.

stem.en:
Text 1
Group projects teach students to share work, listen to each other and settle disagreements, skills they will need in almost any job. For this reason, a teacher should give every group a single grade: the group succeeds or fails together.

Text 2
A single grade for a whole group can be unfair. In many groups, one or two students do most of the work while the others do little. A better system would give each student part of the grade for the group's result and part for his or her own contribution.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the system proposed in Text 2?

options.en: By objecting that it weakens the idea that a group succeeds or fails together
By agreeing that each student's own work should count most
By arguing that group projects should be replaced with individual written tests in every subject
By claiming that students in groups always share the work equally

why.en: Text 1 wants a single grade because 'the group succeeds or fails together'; a split grade goes against that idea.
why.uz: Text 1 yagona baho tarafdori, chunki «the group succeeds or fails together»; boʻlingan baho bu gʻoyaga zid.
why.ru: Text 1 за одну оценку, потому что «the group succeeds or fails together»; раздельная оценка идёт против этой мысли.

stem.en:
Text 1
Beginners on the piano should start with scales and simple finger exercises. Only when their fingers move correctly should they try real songs; otherwise, they learn bad habits that are hard to break later.

Text 2
Many beginners give up the piano within months, because their first lessons are all exercises and no music. Teachers who let students play a simple song in the very first week keep them interested, and exercises can be added as the songs become harder.

Which choice best describes the relationship between the texts?

options.en: Text 2 suggests a different order of lessons than Text 1.
Text 2 gives an example that supports the lesson plan in Text 1.
Text 2 explains why scales are harder to play than songs.
Text 2 argues that beginners do not need a piano teacher at all.

why.en: Text 1 puts exercises first and songs later; Text 2 puts a song in the first week and adds exercises as the songs get harder.
why.uz: Text 1 avval mashqlar, keyin qoʻshiqlar deydi; Text 2 birinchi haftada qoʻshiq chalishni, mashqlarni esa keyinroq qoʻshishni taklif qiladi.
why.ru: Text 1 ставит упражнения первыми, песни потом; Text 2 даёт песню в первую неделю, а упражнения добавляет по мере усложнения песен.

stem.en:
Text 1
Shop owners on Gulzor Avenue oppose the plan to replace one lane of parking with a bicycle lane. Without parking in front of their doors, they say, customers will drive to the big shopping center instead.

Text 2
When a bicycle lane opened on a nearby street last year, the shops there did not lose customers. Many people who had once driven past now rode by slowly, noticed the shop windows and stopped. A street that is easy to visit by bicycle can bring shops new customers.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the shop owners' concern in Text 1?

options.en: By suggesting that the lane could bring the shops new customers
By agreeing that the shops would lose customers to the shopping center
By arguing that the shop owners should move to the big shopping center
By claiming that very few people in the city ride bicycles

why.en: Text 2 gives a nearby street where a bicycle lane did not cost shops customers and even brought new ones, which answers the owners' fear.
why.uz: Text 2 velosiped yoʻlagi doʻkonlarga xaridor yoʻqotmagan, hatto yangisini olib kelgan yaqin koʻchani misol qiladi: bu egalar xavotiriga javob.
why.ru: Text 2 приводит соседнюю улицу, где велодорожка не отняла у магазинов покупателей, а привела новых, — это ответ на страх владельцев.

stem.en:
Text 1
Some teachers have stopped putting grades on essays and write only comments instead. A grade, they argue, ends the conversation: students look at the number and put the essay away, while a comment invites them to rewrite it.

Text 2
Comments alone can leave students unsure where they stand. A student told that her argument "could be stronger" may not know whether she is close to excellent or far from passing. Comments work best when students also know, at least roughly, how their work measures up.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the teachers described in Text 1?

options.en: By accepting the value of comments but arguing that students also need a sense of their level
By agreeing that grades end the conversation and should never be given
By arguing that written comments discourage students from rewriting their essays a second time
By claiming that students ignore both grades and comments on their essays

why.en: Text 2 says comments 'work best when' students also know how their work measures up: comments help, but alone they leave students unsure.
why.uz: Text 2 izohlar «work best when» oʻquvchi oʻz darajasini ham bilganda deydi: izoh foydali, lekin yolgʻiz oʻzi noaniqlik qoldiradi.
why.ru: Text 2: комментарии «work best when» ученик знает и свой уровень. Они полезны, но сами по себе оставляют неясность.

stem.en:
Text 1
Since a new road reached a small mountain village, tourists have come every summer. Families rent out rooms, sell honey and guide hikers, and young people who once left for the cities now find work at home.

Text 2
Tourism has brought money to the village, but much of it leaves again. Most visitors arrive on tours booked in the city, sleep in a guesthouse owned by outsiders and buy little from local families. Whether tourism helps a village depends less on how many visitors come than on who receives what they spend.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the account of tourism in Text 1?

options.en: By noting that much of the money tourists spend does not reach local families
By agreeing that tourism has given every single family in the village a new source of income
By arguing that the new road should be closed to protect the village
By claiming that young people are still leaving the village for the cities

why.en: Text 2 grants that tourism brought money but says 'much of it leaves again': most spending goes to tours and outside owners, not local families.
why.uz: Text 2 turizm pul olib kelganini tan oladi, lekin «much of it leaves again» deydi: pulning koʻpi mahalliy oilalarga emas, begonalarga ketadi.
why.ru: Text 2 признаёт, что туризм принёс деньги, но «much of it leaves again»: большая часть уходит турфирмам и чужим владельцам, а не местным семьям.

stem.en:
Text 1
Every Sunday, the old center of the city is now closed to cars. Supporters call it a gift to residents: children cycle where buses once roared, and cafés fill the streets with tables. The change, they say, shows how much space cars had quietly taken.

Text 2
Car-free Sundays are pleasant for people who live in the center. For those who live on the edges of the city, however, the center is now harder to reach on the one day they are free to visit it, since on Sundays the buses stop at the edge of the closed area. A change that gives space to some residents takes access from others.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the supporters' view in Text 1?

options.en: By noting that what is a gift for some residents is a loss for others
By rejecting the claim that cars take up space in the city center
By arguing that cafés should not put their tables in the streets
By agreeing that the change is a gift to every resident, wherever they live

why.en: Text 2 agrees the Sundays are 'pleasant' for central residents but says people from the edges lose access: a gain for some, a loss for others.
why.uz: Text 2 markazda yashovchilarga yakshanbalar «pleasant» ekanini tan oladi, lekin chekkadagilar markazga yetolmay qoladi: birovga foyda, birovga zarar.
why.ru: Text 2 соглашается, что жителям центра это «pleasant», но жители окраин теряют доступ: одним выгода, другим потеря.

stem.en:
Text 1
Paying children for household chores teaches them that work earns money, a lesson they will need as adults. A child who earns a little for washing the car learns to plan, to save and to spend with care.

Text 2
Paying for chores can teach the wrong lesson. If a child is paid for washing the car, why should she set the table for free? Family tasks are shared because everyone lives in the home, not because someone is paying. Money for extra jobs may be fine; money for ordinary help can turn family life into a business.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1?

options.en: By warning that pay for ordinary help may make family tasks feel like a job
By agreeing that every household task, large or small, should be paid at a fair rate
By arguing that children should never learn how to save money
By claiming that children who are paid soon stop washing the car

why.en: Text 2 says pay for ordinary help 'can turn family life into a business': tasks are shared because everyone lives there, not for money.
why.uz: Text 2 oddiy yordam uchun pul «can turn family life into a business» deydi: uy ishlari pul uchun emas, hamma shu uyda yashagani uchun boʻlinadi.
why.ru: Text 2: плата за обычную помощь «can turn family life into a business». Дела делят, потому что все живут в доме, а не за деньги.

stem.en:
Text 1
Reading aloud to a class, some teachers argue, wastes the time of students who can already read well: they could cover the same pages much faster on their own.

Text 2
Older students can certainly read faster in silence. But when a teacher reads aloud, the class hears how a sentence should sound, where it pauses and which word it leans on, and students who would give up on a difficult book alone stay with it to the end. Speed is not the only measure of reading.

Which choice best describes how Text 2 relates to Text 1?

options.en: Text 2 accepts a point of Text 1 but names other benefits of reading aloud.
Text 2 offers evidence that students read more slowly when they read alone.
Text 2 agrees with Text 1 that reading aloud should stop in older classes.
Text 2 changes the subject from reading to the way teachers speak.

why.en: Text 2 grants that students 'can certainly read faster in silence' (the point of Text 1), then gives other gains of reading aloud.
why.uz: Text 2 oʻquvchilar «can certainly read faster in silence» ekanini tan oladi (Text 1 fikri), keyin ovoz chiqarib oʻqishning boshqa foydalarini aytadi.
why.ru: Text 2 признаёт, что ученики «can certainly read faster in silence» (довод Text 1), а затем называет другие плюсы чтения вслух.

stem.en:
Text 1
Now that phones hold thousands of photographs, the printed family album may seem pointless. Digital pictures cost nothing, never fade and can be shared in seconds.

Text 2
Precisely because a phone holds thousands of photographs, few of them are ever looked at again. A printed album forces a family to choose: twenty pictures from a summer instead of two thousand. That choice is what makes an album worth opening years later.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the claim in Text 1 that printed albums may seem pointless?

options.en: By arguing that the huge number of digital photos is itself a reason to keep printed albums
By agreeing that digital pictures are better than printed ones because they never fade or tear
By claiming that printed photographs cost less than digital ones
By suggesting that families should take more photographs every summer

why.en: Text 1 cites the thousands of photos as a reason albums seem pointless; Text 2 says that very number is why few are seen, so an album helps.
why.uz: Text 1 minglab suratlarni albom keraksizligiga sabab qiladi; Text 2 aynan shu son tufayli suratlar koʻrilmaydi, albom esa tanlashga majbur qiladi deydi.
why.ru: Text 1 приводит тысячи фото как довод против альбомов; Text 2 говорит, что именно из-за этого их не смотрят, а альбом заставляет выбрать.

stem.en:

A school library should be kept quiet for reading. Once group-study tables arrive, the talking spreads, and students who came to read in peace have nowhere else to go.

Text 2
Our school library added group-study tables last year, in a separate room behind a glass door. Students who want to talk use that room, and the main hall stays quiet. The library is now busier than ever, and the readers have not complained.

Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 1 most likely respond to the arrangement described in Text 2?

options.en: By granting that it may answer the concern about talk spreading to readers
By arguing that a busy library is always better than a quiet one
By claiming that the readers in Text 2 must be hiding their complaints
By insisting that students should not be allowed to study in groups anywhere at school

why.en: Text 1 objects that 'the talking spreads'. In Text 2 the talking stays in a separate room, so the arrangement meets that exact concern.
why.uz: Text 1 «the talking spreads» deb eʼtiroz bildiradi. Text 2 da gaplashish alohida xonada qoladi, demak, bu aynan shu xavotirga javob beradi.
why.ru: Text 1 возражает: «the talking spreads». В Text 2 разговоры остаются в отдельной комнате, то есть это решает именно эту проблему.

stem.en:
When Shahnoza joined the school newspaper, she was given the smallest job: checking spelling. She did it carefully every week, and she began to notice which articles readers talked about most. By the end of the year, the editors asked her to write her own column.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: Careful work at a small job led to a bigger role on the newspaper.
Shahnoza did not enjoy checking the spelling of other students' articles every week.
The school newspaper had more writers than it needed.
Readers rarely talked about the articles in the newspaper.

why.en: The text moves from a small job done carefully to the editors offering her a column: careful small work led to a bigger role.
why.uz: Matn puxta bajarilgan kichik ishdan muharrirlar unga ustun taklif qilishigacha boradi: kichik ishga eʼtibor katta rolga olib keldi.
why.ru: Текст идёт от маленькой работы, сделанной тщательно, к тому, что редакторы дают ей колонку: старание привело к большей роли.

He mixes the dough.

stem.en:

Jamshid had been waiting at the bus stop outside his school for twenty minutes, and the rain was getting heavier. He was about to walk home when an old woman with a large umbrella stepped up beside him and, without a word, held it over both of them. When the bus finally came, she nodded and walked away down the street.

Which choice best describes what happens in the text?

options.en: A stranger shares her umbrella with a boy waiting in the rain.
A boy decides to walk home because the bus is late.
An old woman asks a boy for directions to the nearest bus stop in the heavy rain.
A boy lends his umbrella to an old woman at the bus stop.

For weeks Nigora had told everyone that she did not care about the art prize. When the judge read out the winners and her name was not among them, she smiled and clapped with the others. Only later, alone on the walk home, did she let herself kick a stone hard across the road.

Which choice best describes Nigora's feelings in the text?

options.en: She is more disappointed than she lets other people see.
She is glad that one of her closest friends has won the art prize this year.
She is angry with the judge for being unfair to her.
She truly does not care about the result.

why.en: In public she smiles and claps; alone, she kicks a stone hard. Her calm is for show: she is more upset than she lets others see.
why.uz: Odamlar oldida u jilmayib qarsak chaladi; yolgʻiz qolganda toshni qattiq tepadi. Xotirjamligi koʻz uchun: u koʻrsatganidan koʻproq xafa.
why.ru: При всех она улыбается и хлопает, а одна сильно пинает камень. Спокойствие напоказ: она расстроена сильнее, чем показывает.

stem.en:
Most visitors to the old fortress walk straight to the tower for the view. Few notice the narrow staircase beside the gate, which leads down to a cool cellar where soldiers once stored grain and water. The guide says that the cellar, not the tower, is what allowed the fortress to survive long sieges.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: A part of the fortress that visitors overlook was key to its survival.
The tower gives visitors the best view of the land around the fortress.
Soldiers lived in the cellar during the long sieges.
The fortress was built to store grain for nearby towns.

why.en: The text sets the tower visitors seek against the cellar they miss, and ends: the cellar 'allowed the fortress to survive long sieges'.
why.uz: Matn odamlar intiladigan minorani ular eʼtibor bermaydigan yertoʻla bilan qiyoslaydi: aynan yertoʻla qalʼaga uzoq qamallarda omon qolishga imkon bergan.
why.ru: Текст сравнивает башню, к которой идут туристы, с подвалом, который они не замечают: именно подвал помог крепости выдержать долгие осады.

stem.en:
City councils often judge a new park by its size: how many hectares of grass, how many trees planted. Yet a large park behind a busy highway may be used less than a small square on a quiet residential street. What makes a park valuable to a neighborhood is not mainly how big it is but how easily people can reach it in their daily lives.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: A park's value depends more on how easy it is to reach than on its size.
Large parks are always less useful than small squares.
City councils should plant more trees and lay more grass in the parks they already have.
Parks next to highways are noisier than other parks.

why.en: The last sentence states the idea: value comes 'not mainly' from size but from how easily people reach the park. 'Always' goes too far.
why.uz: Asosiy gʻoya oxirgi gapda: bogʻning qadri «not mainly» kattaligida emas, odamlar unga qanchalik oson yetib borishida. «Always» haddan oshadi.
why.ru: Главная мысль — в последнем предложении: ценность парка «not mainly» в размере, а в том, легко ли до него дойти. «Always» — слишком сильно.

stem.en:
The following text is from a short story.

Grandfather Ergash measured everything: the flour for the bread, the water for the garden, the minutes he let the radio play. So when he handed Akmal a bag of seeds and said only, "Plant them wherever you like," Akmal stood still for a long moment, the bag light in his hand, unsure what to do with a freedom his grandfather had never given him before.

Which choice best describes Akmal's reaction in the text?

options.en: He hesitates, surprised to be given a free choice by his strict grandfather.
He is upset that his grandfather has given him so few seeds.
He is excited to plant the seeds at last in the exact spot he had chosen weeks before.
He is confused about how much water the seeds will need.

why.en: Grandfather 'measured everything', so a free choice is new; Akmal 'stood still', 'unsure what to do with a freedom' he never had.
why.uz: Bobo «measured everything», shuning uchun erkin tanlov yangi narsa; Akmal «stood still», ilgari boʻlmagan erkinlik bilan nima qilishni bilmaydi.
why.ru: Дед «measured everything», поэтому свободный выбор — новинка; Акмаль «stood still», не зная, что делать с невиданной свободой.

stem.en:
When the old covered market was rebuilt, the architects kept its narrow side windows instead of adding large panes of glass. Some visitors call the hall gloomy. The architects explain that the small windows keep the stalls cool in summer and that the soft light stops fruit and vegetables from spoiling quickly; the dimness that some visitors dislike is exactly what the market needs.

Which choice best states the main idea of the text?

options.en: A feature of the market that some visitors dislike serves a practical purpose.
The architects now regret that they did not replace the narrow windows with large panes of glass.
Visitors prefer markets that have large panes of glass.
Fruit spoils quickly in markets that have large windows.

why.en: The text ends that the dimness visitors dislike 'is exactly what the market needs': the narrow windows keep it cool and slow spoiling.
why.uz: Matn yoqmagan xiralik «is exactly what the market needs» degan fikr bilan tugaydi: tor derazalar salqinlik beradi, meva tez buzilmaydi.
why.ru: Текст кончается тем, что нелюбимый посетителями полумрак «is exactly what the market needs»: узкие окна дают прохладу и берегут фрукты.
